implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the owning repository's neutral Search evaluation protocol, scorer, documentation and contract tests changed, plus this scope's evidence. No production Search source, sibling repository or publication state was changed.
implementation.evaluationContract: Fifteen development tasks are selected in five balanced categories. Each trial offers Search, rg and ordinary tools with equivalent permissions and budget, records randomized arm order, and separates answer correctness from tool-choice appropriateness.
implementation.scoringContract: The primary score requires answer correctness, valid evidence, required completeness, an accepted tool and zero unsafe actions. Failed, partial, cancelled, budget-limited and intervened trials remain in the denominator; category and aggregate Wilson 95% intervals are null when no trials exist.

gateResults.evidence: The final Release owning-repository suite completed across 21 projects with 1,647 total tests, 1,613 passed, 0 failed and 34 classified skips; the focused Search suite and Search build also passed.
The separate review approved the balanced five-category task selection, randomized all-arm presentation, accepted rg wins, failure retention and explicit no-result state.

Five focused contract tests validate protocol balance, task-set reference and leakage boundary, required trial fields, Wilson intervals and separate choice scoring; the full Search suite and five semantic harnesses also passed.

The scorer validates registered arms, randomized permutations, duplicate trials, non-negative measurements, completeness requirements and the recorded inappropriate-tool flag without inventing Search capabilities.

knownLimitations: No fresh-context agent runner is available in this checkout, so no tool-choice rates, failures or empirical confidence intervals are claimed; the committed scorer returns a null interval for zero trials.
The selected tasks reference the W15-S03 development set. Hidden variants must be generated separately and must not expose expected answers, validator source or hidden fixture material.
Tool appropriateness is evaluated only after answer, evidence and completeness checks; an accepted arm is not a license to make an incomplete negative claim.
Platform-dependent unreadable and invalid-encoding behavior requires evidence from the platform on which future trials run.
No package was published, pushed, released or installed, and no sibling repository was edited.
